ESV.1: “You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits  long and five cubits broad. The altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits.
ESV.2: And you shall make horns for it on its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
ESV.3: You shall make pots for it to receive its ashes, and shovels and basins and forks and fire pans. You shall make all its utensils of bronze.
ESV.4: You shall also make for it a grating, a network of bronze, and on the net you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.
ESV.5: And you shall set it under the ledge of the altar so that the net extends halfway down the altar.
ESV.6: And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
ESV.7: And the poles shall be put through the rings, so that the poles are on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
ESV.8: You shall make it hollow, with boards. As it has been shown you on the mountain, so shall it be made.
ESV.9: “You shall make the court of the tabernacle. On the south side the court shall have hangings of fine twined linen a hundred cubits long for one side.
ESV.10: Its twenty pillars and their twenty bases shall be of bronze, but the hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.
ESV.11: And likewise for its length on the north side there shall be hangings a hundred cubits long, its pillars twenty and their bases twenty, of bronze, but the hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.
ESV.12: And for the breadth of the court on the west side there shall be hangings for fifty cubits, with ten pillars and ten bases.
ESV.13: The breadth of the court on the front to the east shall be fifty cubits.
ESV.14: The hangings for the one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and three bases.
ESV.15: On the other side the hangings shall be fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and three bases.
ESV.16: For the gate of the court there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue and purple and scarlet yarns and fine twined linen, embroidered with needlework. It shall have four pillars and with them four bases.
ESV.17: All the pillars around the court shall be filleted with silver. Their hooks shall be of silver, and their bases of bronze.
ESV.18: The length of the court shall be a hundred cubits, the breadth fifty, and the height five cubits, with hangings of fine twined linen and bases of bronze.
ESV.19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, and all its pegs and all the pegs of the court, shall be of bronze.
ESV.20: “You shall command the people of Israel that they bring to you pure beaten olive oil for the light, that a lamp may regularly be set up to burn.
ESV.21: In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it from evening to morning before the LORD. It shall be a statute forever to be observed throughout their generations by the people of Israel.

NKJV.1: “You shall make an altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide—the altar shall be square—and its height shall be three cubits.
NKJV.2: You shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it. And you shall overlay it with bronze.
NKJV.3: Also you shall make its pans to receive its ashes, and its shovels and its basins and its forks and its firepans; you shall make all its utensils of bronze.
NKJV.4: You shall make a grate for it, a network of bronze; and on the network you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.
NKJV.5: You shall put it under the rim of the altar beneath, that the network may be midway up the altar.
NKJV.6: And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
NKJV.7: The poles shall be put in the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar to bear it.
NKJV.8: You shall make it hollow with boards; as it was shown you on the mountain, so shall they make it.
NKJV.9: “You shall also make the court of the tabernacle. For the south side there shall be hangings for the court made of fine woven linen, one hundred cubits long for one side.
NKJV.10: And its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets shall be bronze. The hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be silver.
NKJV.11: Likewise along the length of the north side there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, with its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of bronze, and the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
NKJV.12: “And along the width of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits, with their ten pillars and their ten sockets.
NKJV.13: The width of the court on the east side shall be fifty cubits.
NKJV.14: The hangings on one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
NKJV.15: And on the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
NKJV.16: “For the gate of the court there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, woven of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, made by a weaver. It shall have four pillars and four sockets.
NKJV.17: All the pillars around the court shall have bands of silver; their hooks shall be of silver and their sockets of bronze.
NKJV.18: The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, the width fifty throughout, and the height five cubits, made of fine woven linen, and its sockets of bronze.
NKJV.19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for all its service, all its pegs, and all the pegs of the court, shall be of bronze.
NKJV.20: “And you shall command the children of Israel that they bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to cause the lamp to burn continually.
NKJV.21: In the tabernacle of meeting, outside the veil which is before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it from evening until morning before the LORD. It shall be a statute forever to their generations on behalf of the children of Israel.

NASB.1: 'And you shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits.
NASB.2: 'You shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
NASB.3: 'You shall make its pails for removing its ashes, and its shovels and its basins and its forks and its firepans; you shall make all its utensils of bronze.
NASB.4: 'You shall make for it a grating of network of bronze, and on the net you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.
NASB.5: 'You shall put it beneath, under the ledge of the altar, so that the net will reach halfway up the altar.
NASB.6: 'You shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
NASB.7: 'Its poles shall be inserted into the rings, so that the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
NASB.8: 'You shall make it hollow with planks; as it was shown to you in the mountain, so they shall make [it].
NASB.9: 'You shall make the court of the tabernacle. On the south side [there shall be] hangings for the court of fine twisted linen one hundred cubits long for one side;
NASB.10: and its pillars [shall be] twenty, with their twenty sockets of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [shall be] of silver.
NASB.11: 'Likewise for the north side in length [there shall be] hangings one hundred [cubits] long, and its twenty pillars with their twenty sockets of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [shall be] of silver.
NASB.12: '[For] the width of the court on the west side [shall be] hangings of fifty cubits [with] their ten pillars and their ten sockets.
NASB.13: 'The width of the court on the east side [shall be] fifty cubits.
NASB.14: 'The hangings for the [one] side [of the gate shall be] fifteen cubits [with] their three pillars and their three sockets.
NASB.15: 'And for the other side [shall be] hangings of fifteen cubits [with] their three pillars and their three sockets.
NASB.16: 'For the gate of the court [there] [shall be] a screen of twenty cubits, of blue and purple and scarlet [material] and fine twisted linen, the work of a weaver, [with] their four pillars and their four sockets.
NASB.17: 'All the pillars around the court shall be furnished with silver bands [with] their hooks of silver and their sockets of bronze.
NASB.18: 'The length of the court [shall be] one hundred cubits, and the width fifty throughout, and the height five cubits of fine twisted linen, and their sockets of bronze.
NASB.19: 'All the utensils of the tabernacle [used] in all its service, and all its pegs, and all the pegs of the court, [shall be] of bronze.
NASB.20: 'You shall charge the sons of Israel, that they bring you clear oil of beaten olives for the light, to make a lamp burn continually.
NASB.21: 'In the tent of meeting, outside the veil which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before the LORD; [it shall be] a perpetual statute throughout their generations for the sons of Israel.

AMP.1: "And you shall make the altar [for burnt offerings] of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits.
AMP.2: Make horns (horn-shaped projections) for it on its four corners; the horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
AMP.3: You shall make pots to remove its ashes, and shovels, basins [to catch the blood of the sacrificed animal], meat-forks, and firepans [to store live coals]. You shall make all its utensils of bronze.
AMP.4: Also make a grate for it, a network of bronze; and on the grid you are to make four bronze rings at its four corners.
AMP.5: And you shall put it under the ledge of the altar, so that the grid will extend halfway up the altar.
AMP.6: You shall make [carrying] poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, overlaid with bronze.
AMP.7: The poles shall be inserted through the rings on the two sides of the altar so that it may be carried.
AMP.8: You are to make the altar hollow with planks; as you were shown on the mountain [of Sinai], so shall it be made.
AMP.9: "You shall make the court of the tabernacle. The south side of the court is to have curtains of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long for one side;
AMP.10: it shall have twenty pillars and twenty bronze sockets; but the hooks of the pillars and their fasteners shall be silver;
AMP.11: likewise for the north side there shall be curtains, a hundred cubits long, and its twenty pillars and twenty bronze sockets; but the hooks of the pillars and their fasteners shall be silver.
AMP.12: For the width of the court on the west side there shall be curtains of fifty cubits, with ten pillars (support poles) and ten sockets.
AMP.13: The width of the court [to the front], on the east side shall be fifty cubits.
AMP.14: The curtains for one side [of the gate] shall be fifteen cubits with three pillars and three sockets.
AMP.15: On the other side [of the gate] the curtains shall be fifteen cubits with three pillars and three sockets.
AMP.16: For the gate of the court there shall be a screen [to provide a covering] of twenty cubits, of blue, purple, and scarlet fabric and finely woven [embroidered] linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four pillars and four [base] sockets.
AMP.17: All the pillars (support poles) around the court shall be joined together with silver rods; their hooks shall be of silver and their sockets of bronze.
AMP.18: The length of the court shall be a hundred cubits, and the width fifty [cubits] throughout, and the height five cubits of fine twisted linen, and their sockets of bronze.
AMP.19: All the tabernacle's utensils and instruments used in all its service, and all its stakes, and all the stakes for the court, shall be of bronze.
AMP.20: "You shall command the Israelites to provide you with clear oil of beaten olives for the light, to make a lamp burn continually [every night].
AMP.21: In the Tent of Meeting [of God with His people], outside the veil which is in front of the [ark of the] Testimony [and sets it apart], Aaron [the high priest] and his sons shall keep the lamp burning from evening to morning before the LORD. It shall be a perpetual statute [to be observed] throughout their generations on behalf of the Israelites.

CSB17.1: “You <sup>ⓝ</sup> are to construct the altar of acacia wood. The altar must be square, 7½ feet long, and 7½ feet wide; <sup>[1]</sup> it must be 4½ feet high. <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.2: Make horns for it on its four corners; the horns are to be of one piece. <sup>[3]</sup> Overlay it with bronze. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.3: Make its pots for removing ashes, and its shovels, basins, meat forks, and firepans; make all its utensils of bronze.
CSB17.4: Construct a grate for it of bronze mesh, and make four bronze rings on the mesh at its four corners.
CSB17.5: Set it below, under the altar’s ledge, <sup>[4]</sup> so that the mesh comes halfway up <sup>[5]</sup> the altar.
CSB17.6: Then make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
CSB17.7: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on two sides of the altar when it is carried.
CSB17.8: Construct the altar with boards so that it is hollow. They are to make it just as it was shown to you on the mountain. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.9: “You <sup>ⓒ</sup> are to make the courtyard for the tabernacle. Make hangings for the south side of the courtyard out of finely spun linen, 150 feet <sup>[6]</sup> long on that side
CSB17.10: including twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and silver bands <sup>[7]</sup> for the posts.
CSB17.11: And so make hangings 150 feet long for the north side, including twenty posts and their twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and silver bands for the posts.
CSB17.12: For the width of the courtyard, make hangings 75 feet <sup>[8]</sup> long for the west side, including their ten posts and their ten bases.
CSB17.13: And for the width of the courtyard on the east side toward the sunrise, 75 feet,
CSB17.14: make hangings 22½ feet <sup>[9]</sup> long for one side of the gate, including their three posts and their three bases.
CSB17.15: And make hangings 22½ feet long for the other side, including their three posts and their three bases.
CSB17.16: The gate of the courtyard is to have a 30-foot <sup>[10]</sup> screen <sup>ⓓ</sup> embroidered <sup>[11]</sup> with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It is to have four posts and their four bases.
CSB17.17: “All the posts around the courtyard are to be banded with silver and have silver hooks and bronze bases.
CSB17.18: The courtyard is to be 150 feet long, 75 feet wide at each end, and 7½ feet high, <sup>[12]</sup> all of it made of finely spun linen. The bases of the posts are to be bronze.
CSB17.19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use and all its tent pegs as well as all the tent pegs of the courtyard are to be made of bronze.
CSB17.20: “You are to command the Israelites to bring you pure oil from crushed olives for the light, in order to keep the lamp burning regularly.
CSB17.21: In the tent of meeting outside the curtain that is in front of the testimony, <sup>ⓔ</sup> Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamp <sup>ⓕ</sup> from evening until morning before the LORD. This is to be a permanent statute <sup>ⓖ</sup> for the Israelites throughout their generations.

NLT.1: “Using acacia wood, construct a square altar 7 1⁄2 feet wide, 7 1⁄2 feet long, and 4 1⁄2 feet high.
NLT.2: Make horns for each of its four corners so that the horns and altar are all one piece. Overlay the altar with bronze.
NLT.3: Make ash buckets, shovels, basins, meat forks, and firepans, all of bronze.
NLT.4: Make a bronze grating for it, and attach four bronze rings at its four corners.
NLT.5: Install the grating halfway down the side of the altar, under the ledge.
NLT.6: For carrying the altar, make poles from acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
NLT.7: Insert the poles through the rings on the two sides of the altar.
NLT.8: The altar must be hollow, made from planks. Build it just as you were shown on the mountain.
NLT.9: “Then make the courtyard for the Tabernacle, enclosed with curtains made of finely woven linen. On the south side, make the curtains 150 feet long.
NLT.10: They will be held up by twenty posts set securely in twenty bronze bases. Hang the curtains with silver hooks and rings.
NLT.11: Make the curtains the same on the north side — 150 feet of curtains held up by twenty posts set securely in bronze bases. Hang the curtains with silver hooks and rings.
NLT.12: The curtains on the west end of the courtyard will be 75 feet long, supported by ten posts set into ten bases.
NLT.13: The east end of the courtyard, the front, will also be 75 feet long.
NLT.14: The courtyard entrance will be on the east end, flanked by two curtains. The curtain on the right side will be 22 1⁄2 feet long, supported by three posts set into three bases.
NLT.15: The curtain on the left side will also be 22 1⁄2 feet long, supported by three posts set into three bases.
NLT.16: “For the entrance to the courtyard, make a curtain that is 30 feet long. Make it from finely woven linen, and decorate it with beautiful embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet thread. Support it with four posts, each securely set in its own base.
NLT.17: All the posts around the courtyard must have silver rings and hooks and bronze bases.
NLT.18: So the entire courtyard will be 150 feet long and 75 feet wide, with curtain walls 7 1⁄2 feet high, made from finely woven linen. The bases for the posts will be made of bronze.
NLT.19: “All the articles used in the rituals of the Tabernacle, including all the tent pegs used to support the Tabernacle and the courtyard curtains, must be made of bronze.
NLT.20: “Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
NLT.21: The lampstand will stand in the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain that shields the Ark of the Covenant. Aaron and his sons must keep the lamps burning in the LORD’s presence all night. This is a permanent law for the people of Israel, and it must be observed from generation to generation.

WEB.1: “You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits  long, and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square: and its height shall be three cubits.
WEB.2: You shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it; and you shall overlay it with brass.
WEB.3: You shall make its pots to take away its ashes, its shovels, its basins, its meat hooks, and its fire pans: all its vessels you shall make of brass.
WEB.4: You shall make a grating for it of network of brass: and on the net you shall make four bronze rings in its four corners.
WEB.5: You shall put it under the ledge around the altar beneath, that the net may reach halfway up the altar.
WEB.6: You shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with brass.
WEB.7: Its poles shall be put into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar, when carrying it.
WEB.8: You shall make it with hollow planks. They shall make it as it has been shown you on the mountain.
WEB.9: “You shall make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined linen one hundred cubits long for one side:
WEB.10: and its pillars shall be twenty, and their sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of silver.
WEB.11: Likewise for the north side in length there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, and its pillars twenty, and their sockets twenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
WEB.12: For the width of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
WEB.13: The width of the court on the east side eastward shall be fifty cubits.
WEB.14: The hangings for the one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
WEB.15: For the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
WEB.16: For the gate of the court shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined linen, the work of the embroiderer; their pillars four, and their sockets four.
WEB.17: All the pillars of the court around shall be filleted with silver; their hooks of silver, and their sockets of brass.
WEB.18: The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, and the width fifty every where, and the height five cubits, of fine twined linen, and their sockets of brass.
WEB.19: All the instruments of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its pins, and all the pins of the court, shall be of brass.
WEB.20: “You shall command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.
WEB.21: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before Yahweh: it shall be a statute forever throughout their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.

NRSVCE.1: You shall make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square, and it shall be three cubits high.
NRSVCE.2: You shall make horns for it on its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
NRSVCE.3: You shall make pots for it to receive its ashes, and shovels and basins and forks and firepans; you shall make all its utensils of bronze.
NRSVCE.4: You shall also make for it a grating, a network of bronze; and on the net you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.
NRSVCE.5: You shall set it under the ledge of the altar so that the net shall extend halfway down the altar.
NRSVCE.6: You shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze;
NRSVCE.7: the poles shall be put through the rings, so that the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
NRSVCE.8: You shall make it hollow, with boards. They shall be made just as you were shown on the mountain.
NRSVCE.9: You shall make the court of the tabernacle. On the south side the court shall have hangings of fine twisted linen one hundred cubits long for that side;
NRSVCE.10: its twenty pillars and their twenty bases shall be of bronze, but the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
NRSVCE.11: Likewise for its length on the north side there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, their pillars twenty and their bases twenty, of bronze, but the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
NRSVCE.12: For the width of the court on the west side there shall be fifty cubits of hangings, with ten pillars and ten bases.
NRSVCE.13: The width of the court on the front to the east shall be fifty cubits.
NRSVCE.14: There shall be fifteen cubits of hangings on the one side, with three pillars and three bases.
NRSVCE.15: There shall be fifteen cubits of hangings on the other side, with three pillars and three bases.
NRSVCE.16: For the gate of the court there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and crimson yarns, and of fine twisted linen, embroidered with needlework; it shall have four pillars and with them four bases.
NRSVCE.17: All the pillars around the court shall be banded with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their bases of bronze.
NRSVCE.18: The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, the width fifty, and the height five cubits, with hangings of fine twisted linen and bases of bronze.
NRSVCE.19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for every use, and all its pegs and all the pegs of the court, shall be of bronze.
NRSVCE.20: You shall further command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the light, so that a lamp may be set up to burn regularly.
NRSVCE.21: In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that is before the covenant, Aaron and his sons shall tend it from evening to morning before the LORD. It shall be a perpetual ordinance to be observed throughout their generations by the Israelites.

NIV.1:
The Altar of Burnt Offering
“Build an altar of acacia wood, three cubits high; it is to be square, five cubits long and five cubits wide.
NIV.2: Make a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar are of one piece, and overlay the altar with bronze.
NIV.3: Make all its utensils of bronze—its pots to remove the ashes, and its shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans.
NIV.4: Make a grating for it, a bronze network, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the network.
NIV.5: Put it under the ledge of the altar so that it is halfway up the altar.
NIV.6: Make poles of acacia wood for the altar and overlay them with bronze.
NIV.7: The poles are to be inserted into the rings so they will be on two sides of the altar when it is carried.
NIV.8: Make the altar hollow, out of boards. It is to be made just as you were shown on the mountain.
NIV.9:
The Courtyard
“Make a courtyard for the tabernacle. The south side shall be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains of finely twisted linen,
NIV.10: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
NIV.11: The north side shall also be a hundred cubits long and is to have curtains, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
NIV.12: “The west end of the courtyard shall be fifty cubits wide and have curtains, with ten posts and ten bases.
NIV.13: On the east end, toward the sunrise, the courtyard shall also be fifty cubits wide.
NIV.14: Curtains fifteen cubits long are to be on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases,
NIV.15: and curtains fifteen cubits long are to be on the other side, with three posts and three bases.

NIV.17: All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and hooks, and bronze bases.
NIV.18: The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with curtains of finely twisted linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.

NIV.20:
Oil for the Lampstand
“Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light so that the lamps may be kept burning.
NIV.21: In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to keep the lamps burning before the Lord from evening till morning. This is to be a lasting ordinance among the Israelites for the generations to come.
